In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aconitase was the key enzyme for the reduction of citrate in both mitochondria and cytosol and citrate synthase played a key role for citric acid accumulation in the mitochondria.

citrate synthase, aconitases in both mitochondrial andcytosolic fractions and IDH in cytosolic fractions were important enzymes for citric acid accumulation and reduction at the early and late growth stages of tangerine fruit, respectively.

citrate synthase was the first key enzyme for citric acid accumulation in mitochondria at early growth stage, and aconitases in both mitochondria and cytoplasm and NADP- IDH in cytoplasm were the main enzymes for citric acid reduction in both mitochondria, cytosol and vacuole during fruit maturation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the citric acid accumulation was due to the induction of citrate synthases in mitochondria, whereas its decline was attributed to the induction of aconitases in cytosol.

the citric acid accumulation at the early growth stage of both cultivars was due to the high citrate synthase enzyme in the mitochondrial fraction and the low aconitase enzyme in the cytosolic fraction.

citrate synthase is a key enzyme for citric acid accumulation in mitochondria, aconitases in cytosol and mitochondria play a role in citric acid reduction and the activity of cytosolic aconitase could account for the differences in citric acid contents between the two cultivar.
The main takeaway from our work is that
citric acid content in citrus fruits is controlled by citrate synthase, aconitases and NADPIDH.
aconitase enzyme activity in both cytosol and mitochondria is important to citric acid accumulation and its decline in citrus fruits.
